design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of summit_miles_status_and_upgrades (category loyalty). Frozen 2026-10-06 09:40:00 CDT.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
Marisol Ibarra (Summit Platinum) asks only to buy exactly the miles she is short for the miles upgrades waitlisted on her Frankfurt round trip, and to pay for them herself. The scored number is the purchase price, which rests on the miles bought, which rests on her balance at handling time. The purchase policy states that the miles are worked out only after every selection of bonus miles carries its bonus credit, not until every cleared miles upgrade carries its charge, and that the purchase is recorded only after every selection of upgrade certificates carries its issue. Her records show all three unfulfilled: the 2026-02-10 bonus-miles selection (year 2025) was never credited, the Atlanta outbound upgraded with miles at the gate on 2026-09-29 was never charged, and the 2026-01-28 certificate selection (year 2024) was never issued. The agent must read these out of the prerequisite sentences and the activity and waitlist records, compute each owed posting (bonus 29500 miles, co-pay 12.00 with 25000 miles, 13 certificates), and only then compute the purchase (20000 miles for 440.00) and hand it to the caller. Skipping the bonus makes her buy 49000 miles for 1078.00; skipping the charge makes the purchase unnecessary (0.00). Every number is a multi-factor calculation over history (selection dates, flight accruals and certificate redemptions of the last twelve months, earlier purchases, waitlist and clearances) and over four other products (companion card-anniversary certificate, Summit Club, seat pass, tickets and their coupons).

2. SCOPE AND SPACE BUDGET (principle C)
Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5, 6]}. Occupied by task 0: loyalty_ext_retro_credit_miles, loyalty_ext_retro_segment_qualifying_dollars, loyalty_ext_tier_requalification, loyalty_ext_reinstatement_fee and their four tools. Task 1 claims loyalty_ext_choice_bonus_miles (4 factors), loyalty_ext_miles_upgrade_charge (5), loyalty_ext_choice_upgrade_certificates (5), loyalty_ext_upgrade_topup_purchase (6) — multiset {4,5,5,6} equals the draw — with post_choice_bonus_miles_029b6e8c, post_miles_upgrade_charge_7f00044a, issue_choice_upgrade_certificates_458899d3 and buy_miles_4af9ade8 (owner=user). No policy or tool is shared with task 0; task 1 is the last task, so no headroom remains to reserve and all eight policies are covered.

3. POLICIES, TRIGGERS, LINEAGE, OVERWRITES
- loyalty_ext_choice_bonus_miles: state_due, subject loyalty_bonus_credit, refs loyalty_choice_benefits + loyalty_goodwill_and_bonus (both govern the subject). Overwrite of 'bonus_miles, which credits choice_bonus_miles_per_selection miles'. The open-membership gate and 'bonus credits never count as qualifying activity' stay inherited (the tool does not move last_activity_date).
- loyalty_ext_miles_upgrade_charge: state_due, subject loyalty_award_redemption, refs loyalty_award_redemptions (governing) + loyalty_upgrades_policy (miles cost lineage). Overwrite of 'plus miles_upgrade_copay_usd per segment'. The miles stay the base cost (25000 above the 1000-mile threshold); redeem_active and 'miles cannot go negative' stay inherited; the upgrade kind triggers no ticket booking (only saver and standard do).
- loyalty_ext_choice_upgrade_certificates: state_due, subject loyalty_certificate_issue, refs loyalty_choice_benefits + loyalty_upgrades_policy. Overwrite of 'upgrade_certificates, which issues choice_upgrade_certificates_per_selection Summit Upgrade Certificates'; expiry after certificate_validity_months stays.
- loyalty_ext_upgrade_topup_purchase: on_request, subject loyalty_miles_purchase, refs loyalty_miles_purchases + loyalty_upgrades_policy. Overwrite of 'at miles_purchase_price_per_1000_usd for each thousand miles' for top-up purchases; increments, minimum, annual cap (20000 + 5000 this year far below 150000) and open-membership gate stay.

4. FACTOR CARD
Bonus credit = 29500 (all-baseline 20000):
- late_posting_treatment (method, history+date): selection 2026-02-10, 238 days -> x1.25 rounded up to the thousand = 25000; baseline 24500.
- bonus_card_bonus (parameter, companion, multi-source): First certificate issued 2026-05-18 -> 10 percent = 2000; baseline 27500.
- flown_segment_bonus (parameter, history): 9 flight accruals in the last twelve months -> 1500; baseline 28000. Near-miss: the 2024-06 Sydney accruals are outside the window.
- tenure_bonus (parameter, date): 7 whole years since 2019-03-15 -> 1000; baseline 28500.
Upgrade co-pay = 12.00 (all-baseline 50.00):
- copay_share (parameter, ticket): Crestline Main Plus -> 75 percent -> 37.50; baseline 30.00.
- distance_treatment (method, history+ticket): 1199 miles > 1000 (<= 2000) -> x1.5 rounded up -> 57; baseline 0.00.
- card_copay_reduction (parameter, companion, multi-source): 20; baseline 32.00.
- clearance_timing_reduction (parameter, history+ticket): cleared 2026-09-29, segment 1 flown 2026-09-29 -> 10; baseline 22.00. Near-miss: segment 2 of the same ticket flew 2026-10-03 (4 days, no reduction) and is not the upgraded segment.
- lounge_copay_reduction (parameter, club, multi-source): Executive active -> 15; baseline 27.00.
- Near-miss for the charge object: the two certificate clearances of 2025 are not miles upgrades.
Certificate issue = 13 (all-baseline 4):
- late_issue_treatment (method): 251 days -> 4 x 1.5 = 6; baseline 11.
- card_certificate_award (parameter, companion, multi-source): 2; baseline 11.
- premium_flyer_award (parameter, ticket history): 3 First coupons in twelve months -> 1; baseline 12. Near-miss: the 2025-10-20 outbound flew Premium Economy.
- lounge_certificate_award (parameter, club, multi-source): 2; baseline 11.
- certificate_user_award (parameter, history): 2 redemptions in twelve months -> 2; baseline 11. Near-miss: the 2026-01-21 expiry is not a redemption.
Top-up price = 440.00 (all-baseline 700.00):
- elite_purchase_price (parameter, tier+date, multi-source): Platinum valid -> 30.00; baseline 523.60.
- repeat_buyer_treatment (method, history): one purchase (2026-03-05) in twelve months -> x0.95 to the cent = 28.50; baseline 466.40.
- lounge_price_reduction (parameter, club, multi-source): 2.00; baseline 475.20.
- departure_cabin_reduction (parameter, ticket + waitlist, multi-source over two records): the Frankfurt ticket departs 2026-10-22 (16 days, within 21) AND its latest miles request asks for First -> 1.50; baseline 466.40. Its fall-through (a trip departing more than 21 days out) is reachable by any in-scope customer.
- card_purchase_discount (parameter, companion, multi-source): 10 percent; baseline 490.00.
- subscription_purchase_discount (parameter, pass, multi-source): Seat Pass Network active -> 2 percent; baseline 450.00.
Cross-difficulty evidence seeded: companion CMP37720519 (+ grant), club SC300774415 (+ dues and guest-pass grant), pass SP300455187 (+ term charge), twelve tickets and nine coupons of the last twelve months. The Atlanta clearance's miles_used 0 / copay_usd 0 are stale stamps that no rule reads.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD
- bonus credit (step 14): loyalty_goodwill_and_bonus.goodwill_open_membership (status active); loyalty_choice_benefits has no gate on the credit (policy_scope). The selection itself (2026-02-10) was accepted inside the Platinum year-2025 validity with the count below choice_benefits_count 1.
- upgrade charge (step 16): loyalty_award_redemptions.redeem_active (status active); balance 26300 or 55800 covers 25000 in either order.
- certificate issue (step 18): loyalty_choice_benefits has no gate on the issue (policy_scope); the selection of 2026-01-28 was made before the year-2024 validity ended on 2026-01-31.
- purchase (step 20): loyalty_miles_purchases.purchase_open_membership (status active). No time gate applies to any of the four subjects (temporal_feasibility is empty).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Bonus: the latest selection of bonus miles (2026-02-10, year 2025); the 2025-01-20 and 2026-01-28 selections are certificates. Charge: the latest miles clearance (Atlanta ticket, segment 1, request of 1199 miles); certificate clearances excluded. Issue: the latest certificate selection (2026-01-28, year 2024); the year-2023 selection already has its 2025-01-20 issue. Purchase: the Frankfurt ticket of the latest miles request, its two requests with no clearance.

7. PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root loyalty_ext_upgrade_topup_purchase. Edges (all state form):
- purchase -> bonus (value_input, gate member_balance): 'The miles a top-up purchase buys are worked out only after every choice selection of bonus miles on the membership carries its bonus credit.' (affirmative). False at opening: selection 2026-02-10 has no bonus credit. Only the bonus-credit posting writes a bonus credit for a selection.
- purchase -> upgrade charge (value_input, gate member_balance): 'The miles a top-up purchase buys are not worked out until every miles upgrade that has cleared on the membership carries its miles charge on the membership's activity.' (negated). False at opening: the 2026-09-29 miles clearance has no redemption. Only the upgrade-charge posting writes it.
- purchase -> certificate issue (state_gate, gate loyalty_activity.event_type): 'A top-up purchase is recorded only after every choice selection of upgrade certificates on the membership carries its certificate issue.' (affirmative). False at opening: the 2026-01-28 selection has no issue. Only the certificate-issue posting writes it.
Fan-out; the three writes commute (six orders run, identical values and terminal hash). Customer's own write: the purchase (owner=user), handed over last.

8. PERSONA DESIGN
Brisk, organised procurement director; one-line opener about buying exactly the miles short for the Frankfurt miles upgrades; pays herself. Locator 7205553416; verification DOB 1983-11-02 (email or ZIP as alternatives); Summit number on request; trip detail on request. Conditional cooperation when the agent says something must be settled first; natural reactions if the agent raises the Atlanta gate upgrade or earlier choice benefits; completes the purchase with the handed-over details and closes.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION RUN
Reads: customer -> verify -> membership -> activity (69) -> upgrades (8) -> tickets (12) -> coupons (9) -> companion + ledger -> club + ledger -> pass + ledger. Writes: bonus 29500 (year 2025) -> upgrade charge Atlanta seg 1: 25000 miles, 12.00 -> 13 certificates (year 2024, expiring 2027-10-06) -> member buys 20000 miles for 440.00.
Harness run (summit_d3/t1_gold.py):
  bonus => 29500 | {late 24500, card 27500, segments 28000, tenure 28500} | all 20000
  co-pay => 12.0 | {share 30.0, distance 0.0, card 32.0, timing 22.0, lounge 27.0} | all 50.0
  certificates => 13 | {late 11, card 11, flyer 12, lounge 11, user 11} | all 4
  price => 440.0 | {elite 523.6, buyer 466.4, lounge 475.2, cabin 466.4, card 490.0, pass 450.0} | all 700.0
  skip bonus -> 49000 miles, 1078.0; skip charge -> 0 miles, 0.0; skip issue -> 440.0 (state gate).
  all six orders of the three prerequisites -> identical values and terminal hash.
  receipts: bonus balance 55800; charge balance 30800; certificates 13; purchase balance 50800.

10. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
From the published rules alone: the purchase sentences point at the unfulfilled bonus selection, the uncharged clearance and the unissued certificate selection; each owed posting's rule prices it (29500; 12.00 on 25000 miles; 13); the purchase rule then costs the two Frankfurt requests at 25000 each, subtracts the 30800 balance, rounds 19200 up to 20000 and prices it at 25.00 per thousand less 12 percent = 440.00. Same writes, same numbers as gold.

11. REVISIONS
- The first ledger draft went negative before several awards; redemptions re-planned (running minimum 4000) and the last card statement closes the ledger on 26300.
- The clearance-timing factor first read the latest coupon of the ticket (the return leg, 4 days later) and was decorative; it now reads the coupon of the cleared segment.
- The upgrade-charge distance read moved from LATEST to MAX over the one request (same value) so the gate's history-zeroing test sees the aggregate.

12. GATES (run from the repository root)
Per task (--task 1): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (21 actions, closure 107/107); SOLVABILITY OK (verify True, 4 calls, 5 base gates, 78 seed rows); COMPUTE OK (4 computations, 20 factors, 12 cross-difficulty, 20 history rows, 70 branches); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK.
Difficulty-wide: all green as recorded for task 0 (history max 20 >= 8, branches max 84 >= 5, means 77/21 >= 4/4).
Cross-task obligations checked by hand on this world: every ticket names the membership (no retro credit owed), every flown segment carries its qualifying dollars, and the tier count of the requalification policy (2620 x 1.05 = 2751 + 1500 + 200 + 500 = 4951) stays below the Platinum held, so no tier change is owed.

13. ROUND 2 REWORK (audit audits/policy_task/summit_miles_status_and_upgrades, round 1)
- F-1 / T1-1 (rate ladders labelled method): late_posting_treatment: over 180 days scales x1.25 (rounded up to the thousand), 31-180 days adds the flat late_near_bonus_miles 1000, otherwise unchanged. distance_treatment: over twice the threshold adds the flat very_long_surcharge_usd 40, over the threshold scales x1.5 (rounded up to the dollar), otherwise unchanged. repeat_buyer_treatment: two or more earlier purchases take the flat repeat_buyer_reduction_usd 3 off the elite price, exactly one scales it x0.95 (to the cent), otherwise unchanged. The tiers taken here are unchanged, so every gold value is unchanged.
- F-2 / T1-2 (vacuous fall-through): upgrade_cabin_reduction replaced by departure_cabin_reduction. Its tiers combine the trip ticket's scheduled departure (within close_trip_days 21 of the purchase) with the cabin of the latest waitlisted miles request; the fall-through is a trip departing more than 21 days out, which any in-scope customer can reach. Same values on this world (1.50 per thousand; baseline 466.40).
- F-3 / T1-3 (no multi-source factor): departure_cabin_reduction is multi-source over two distinct records (ticket_holdings.next_departure_at of the trip ticket AND loyalty_upgrades.target_cabin of the request), on both non-fall-through tiers.
- O-4: lounge_copay_reduction, lounge_certificate_award, lounge_price_reduction and subscription_purchase_discount no longer claim cross_difficulty; ticket and companion factors remain.
- O-3: docstring wording fixed. Persona O-A: 'not a round number' replaced by 'whatever quantity that comes to'; O-B: 'charge it the normal way' replaced by 'go ahead and put that through'.
- Harness re-run after the rework: 29500 / 12.00 / 13 / 440.00; baselines 24500,27500,28000,28500 / 30,0,32,22,27 / 11,11,12,11,11 / 523.6,466.4,475.2,466.4,490,450; skips 1078.00 / 0.00 / 440.00; all six orders identical.
- Observations kept as recorded: O-C (state-gate edge carries no value by design; max(3-1,1)=2 value_input edges remain), O-D / O-6 (the unfulfilled selections and the uncharged clearance are the seeded unmet states the tree rests on).

14. ROUND 3 REWORK (audit revision_2; task verdict PASS)
- No factor of this task changed tier or value. O-9 touches distance_treatment's very-long tier only (surcharge capped at the shared co-pay); this world stays on the 1x-2x tier (57), so the co-pay is still 12.00 and distance_treatment's baseline figure still 0.00.
- O-8: miles_short has its own compute_basis entry now.
- Re-run: 29500 / 12.00 / 13 / 440.00; sensitivities, skips and the six orders unchanged.

16. ROUND 5 (render-layer source miss SLM-1 / SLM-2; compute untouched, so every figure is unchanged)
- SLM-1, loyalty_ext_miles_upgrade_charge: baseline.rule defines the shared co-pay (tier miles_upgrade_copay_usd times the co-pay share percent, standard_copay_share_percent) and the co-pay to charge (the shared co-pay). copay_share sets the co-pay share percent; distance_treatment sets the co-pay to charge from the shared co-pay before any amount is taken off; the card, clearance-timing and lounge reductions are each taken off the co-pay to charge and never take it below zero.
- SLM-1, loyalty_ext_upgrade_topup_purchase: baseline.rule defines the tier price per thousand (miles_purchase_price_per_1000_usd) and the net price per thousand (the tier price per thousand), and the standard price (miles bought in thousands times the net price per thousand, to the cent). elite_purchase_price sets the tier price per thousand; repeat_buyer_treatment sets the net price per thousand from it before any per-thousand amount is taken off; the lounge and departure-cabin reductions are taken off the net price per thousand; the card and subscription discounts are percents of the price, all percentage discounts added together and taken off once before rounding to the cent.
- SLM-2, purchase price: the overwrite's replaced_by now covers every purchase the retired base clause covered: 'A top-up purchase is priced from the miles bought and the net price per thousand by the rules below and rounded to the cent, and a purchase that covers no waitlisted miles upgrade is priced at miles_purchase_price_per_1000_usd for each thousand miles, outside this rule.' The seeded 2026-03-05 ordinary purchase (5000 miles, 175.00) agrees with it.
- Unchanged: compute, params, every ladder condition, prerequisite sentences. Harness re-run: 29500 / 12.00 / 13 / 440.00; sensitivities, baselines, skips and the six orders identical.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Ibarra, 42, a procurement director in Denver and a Summit Platinum member who flies a lot for work. You are brisk, organised and cheerful, and you like to get things done in one call. Later this month you are flying Crestline to Frankfurt and back, and you already put both flights on the waitlist for an upgrade to First paid with miles. The Crestline app now warns you that your miles will not cover those upgrades if they clear, and you want to fix that today. You open with: "Hi, I've waitlisted miles upgrades on my Frankfurt trip and the app says I don't have enough miles to cover them. I'd like to buy exactly the miles I'm short, today."

You want to buy only what the airline says you need for those Frankfurt upgrades, whatever quantity that comes to, and you will pay for the purchase yourself with the card on file. You do not know how many miles you are short or what they will cost, you never guess a figure, and you accept the quantity and the price the agent gives you. When the agent asks how to find your account you give your mobile number, 7205553416. To verify you, you give your date of birth, 1983-11-02; if they want something else you can also give your email, marisol.ibarra@outlook.com, or your billing ZIP code, 80238. Your Summit number is 3172904458 if they ask. If the agent asks which trip you mean, it is the Denver to Frankfurt round trip at the end of October, both directions waitlisted for First.

If the agent tells you that something on your account has to be settled or posted before the purchase can be worked out, you say that is fine and that they should go ahead and take care of it. If the agent mentions the upgrade you got at the gate on your Atlanta trip at the end of September, you say "oh right, they moved me up at the gate — sure, go ahead and put that through." If the agent mentions choice benefits you selected earlier in the year, you say you had assumed those had gone through, and that they should post whatever you are owed.

When the agent tells you how many miles to buy and the price and hands the purchase over to you, you complete it yourself right away with exactly the details the agent gives you, and then read back what you see. Once the purchase shows on your account, you thank the agent and end the call. If the agent asks whether there is anything else, you say no, that covers it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel (a fan-out under the purchase). Executed run (summit_d3/t1_gold.py) over all six orders of bonus credit, upgrade charge and certificate issue: every order gives bonus 29500, co-pay 12.00, certificates 13, price 440.00 and the identical terminal DB hash. They commute because no computation reads what another writes (the bonus reads selection dates, the card, flight accruals and tenure; the charge reads the clearance, the ticket, the card and the club; the issue reads selection dates, the card, coupons, the club and certificate redemptions) and the balance changes are additive; the charge never takes the balance below zero in either order (26300 or 55800 against 25000).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the bonus credit (step 14) leaves the balance at 1300 after the charge: miles short 48700, miles bought 49000, price 1078.00 instead of 440.00; the terminal lacks the bonus entry.
Skipping the upgrade charge (step 16) leaves the balance at 55800, which covers the 50000 needed: nothing to buy, price 0.00 instead of 440.00; the terminal lacks the redemption entry.

state_gate: skipping the certificate issue (step 18) leaves the purchase figures unchanged (440.00) but the terminal lacks the certificate issue entry and upgrade_certificate_balance stays 0 instead of 13, so the terminal hash differs.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to buy the miles short for the Frankfurt upgrades. It never mentions a bonus, certificates, choice benefits or the Atlanta upgrade on its own; those appear only as conditional reactions after the agent raises them. No prerequisite problem id appears in it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: post_choice_bonus_miles_029b6e8c, post_miles_upgrade_charge_7f00044a, issue_choice_upgrade_certificates_458899d3 and buy_miles_4af9ade8 each read the membership row only for its customer_id and running totals, then ctx.create/ctx.update exactly the values passed; none inspects selections, clearances, balances or certificates, none refuses or errors, so the purchase can be booked at any quantity before the prerequisites are resolved.
